nodes.name: Cleaning of Cu foam
nodes.procedure: 3 × 4 cm2 CF was cleaned using a 1.0 M HCl solution and deionised water by ultrasonication for several times.
nodes.source_text: Prior to the chemical oxidation, 3 × 4 cm2 CF was cleaned using a 1.0 M HCl solution and deionised water by ultrasonication for several times.

nodes.name: Chemical oxidation to Cu(OH)2 NWs
nodes.procedure: The cleaned CF was then immersed into a 100 mL aqueous solution containing 10.0 g NaOH and 3.4 g (NH4)2S2O8 for 30 min at room temperature and ambient pressure to form Cu(OH)2 NWs/CF.
nodes.source_text: The cleaned CF was then immersed into a 100 mL aqueous solution containing 10.0 g NaOH and 3.4 g (NH4)2S2O8 for 30 min at room temperature and ambient pressure.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reduction to Cu NWs
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared Cu(OH)2 NWs/CF was reduced to Cu NWs on CF (noted as Cu/CF) through an electrochemical method using a 0.5 M Ar-saturated KHCO3 solution (pH = 7.3) at -1.1 V against SCE for 120 min under a three-electrode system. Argon gas was purged into the solution during the electrochemical reduction.

nodes.name: Magnetron sputtering of WC on Cu NWs
nodes.procedure: The WC layer was deposited on Cu/CF through magnetron sputtering by using an ETD-900 M ion sputtering apparatus (Beijing Elaborate Technology Development Co., China) under Ar atmosphere (15 sccm) at room temperature. The WC target was 50 mm in diameter with a thickness of 2.5 mm, and the distance between WC target and Cu/CF was adjusted to 15 cm. The processing current was controlled at 40 mA with a chamber pressure of 4×10-1 Pa for 720 s. Subsequently, the Cu NWs@WC layer, which was self-supported on CF (noted as Cu@WC-720), was successfully synthesised.

nodes.source_text: Then, the WC layer was deposited on Cu/CF through magnetron sputtering... The processing current was controlled at 40 mA with a chamber pressure of 4×10-1 Pa for 180, 360, 540, 720, 900 and 1080 s.

nodes.name: Direct WC sputtering on CF
nodes.procedure: The WC layer was directly sputtered onto CF through the same magnetron sputtering process.
nodes.source_text: Thereafter, the WC layer was directly sputtered onto CF (noted as WC/CF) through the same magnetron sputtering process.

nodes.description: HER performance in acidic 0.5 M H₂SO₄
nodes.source_text: Cu@WC exhibited the best HER performance with the lowest overpotential 92 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² in 0.5 M H₂SO₄. The Tafel slope of Cu@WC was calculated as 50.5 mV dec⁻¹. The exchange current densities (j₀) of Cu@WC... was approximately 0.50 mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Cu@WC had η₁₀ increased from 92 mV to 119 mV (basic condition). The Tafel slopes of Cu@WC were 88.7 mV dec⁻¹ in the KOH solution.

nodes.description: HER performance in neutral 1.0 M PBS
nodes.source_text: Cu@WC had η₁₀ increased from 92 mV to 119 mV (basic condition) and 173 mV (neutral condition). The Tafel slopes of Cu@WC were 118.3 mV dec⁻¹ in the PBS solution.

nodes.description: HER stability testing at 10 mA/cm² in pH-universal electrolytes
nodes.source_text: Cu@WC exhibited excellent stability at 10 mA cm⁻² over 12 h with almost no attenuation.
